page: Amazon Web Services c3.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The instance is equipped with 15.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.88 GB of RAM per core. It includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and operates on the Xen hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear division between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is generally weak, with Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% and stress-ng single-core CPU performance in the bottom 25%. However, multi-core execution is more robust, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU score, and PassMark database operations all registering in the average range. Memory bandwidth across both cached and uncached read/write operations also maintains average tier performance.

From a resource density perspective, the instance offers a low memory-to-vCPU ratio, which is characteristic of older-generation compute-optimized hardware. While the inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage provides low-latency local disk access, the lack of modern instruction sets like AVX-512 limits its efficiency for advanced vector math or modern machine learning workloads, as evidenced by poor performance in 7B LLM text generation. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option primarily for legacy multi-threaded workloads that do not require modern CPU instructions.

The c3.2xlarge is suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, static web serving, and basic database operations. It is less appropriate for single-threaded tasks, modern large language model inference, or memory-intensive applications.
